title: Pool Spin Explained: Follow, Draw and English for Beginners
description: Learn how follow, draw, stun and English change what the cue ball does, with a simple practice plan to start controlling it today.
body:
Ever watch a pro send the cue ball zipping backward across the table like it is on a string? That is not magic. It is spin, and with a little practice you can start using it too. With the Mosconi Cup coming to Orlando November 27-30, it is the perfect time to learn what the cue ball is really doing.

Where you hit the cue ball changes everything

Picture the cue ball as a clock face or a target. Where your tip touches it decides how the ball behaves after it hits the object ball. There are four basic reactions every player should know: stop, stun, follow and draw.

  • Center ball: hit the middle and the cue ball rolls naturally.
  • Above center (follow): topspin that pushes the cue ball forward after contact.
  • Below center (draw): backspin that pulls the cue ball back toward you.
  • Left or right of center (English): sidespin that changes angles and how the ball comes off a rail.

Stun: the shot that explains the rest

A stun shot is when the cue ball is sliding, with no real topspin or backspin, at the moment it hits the object ball. After contact it does not follow or draw. It leaves along what players call the tangent line, which is roughly 90 degrees from the path of the object ball on a cut shot. Understanding stun gives you a baseline. Follow makes the cue ball bend forward from that line, and draw makes it bend backward.

Follow: easy and very useful

To play a follow shot, aim a tip or so above the center of the cue ball and keep your stroke smooth. On a straight shot, the cue ball keeps rolling forward after the object ball drops. On a cut shot, a rolling cue ball tends to leave at about 30 degrees from the path of the object ball, which is a handy rule of thumb for planning your next shot.

Follow is also the friendliest spin to learn. You do not need to hit it very hard. You only need a straight stroke and a clean finish.

Draw: the crowd pleaser

Draw is where beginners get excited, and where many get frustrated. Strike below center, keep your cue level and follow all the way through the ball. The most common mistakes are slowing down at contact and not hitting low enough. Think of accelerating through the shot rather than poking at the cue ball.

  • Start with short distances, with the cue ball and object ball only a few inches apart.
  • Use a firm, level cue. A raised back end can cause a miscue.
  • Chalk before every shot, because low hits need a good grip.

English: add it last

English is sidespin, created by hitting the cue ball left or right of center. It is the hardest spin to control, because it can change the cue ball angle off rails and even nudge your aim, which is called cue ball deflection. Many coaches suggest beginners build a solid stance, a straight stroke and good center-ball hitting first, then learn follow and draw, and only then add English.

When you are ready, start small. Use the tiniest amount of side spin you can, notice how the cue ball reacts off the rail, and write down what you learn. Over time you will build a feel for it.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Swerving the cue: a straight, level stroke matters far more than power.
  • Hitting too hard: extra speed hides errors for a moment, then ruins position. Control beats force.
  • Skipping chalk: a slick tip is the fastest way to a miscue, especially on draw and English.
  • Changing too many things at once: adjust one thing, such as tip position, and see what happens.

A simple practice plan

  1. Stop shot: shoot a straight shot and try to stop the cue ball where the object ball was.
  2. Follow: repeat from the same spot and make the cue ball roll forward about a diamond.
  3. Draw: repeat again and bring the cue ball back about a diamond.
  4. Mix it up: alternate all three and count how many you hit as planned out of 10.

Ten minutes of this before a game will do more for your position play than a hundred hard breaks. For more drills and lessons, browse our pool guides.

Watch it done by the best

The best way to see spin in action is to watch the pros. Take a look at our Mosconi Cup 2026 hub for dates, start times and how to watch, and notice how often the cue ball seems to land in perfect position. That is follow, draw and stun at work. Want to catch live pool near you? Check the tournament finder, the calendar or the this weekend page, and see the biggest events on big tournaments.

Quick recap

Hit above center to follow, below center to draw, and to the side for English. Master stop, follow and draw at short range first, then slowly add sidespin. Be patient, stay smooth and have fun with it.
